paraphrase: For those established in the generation stage and longing for the completion stage, this method was made by the perfect buddhas like a staircase.

paraphrase: The wind, which is the life of beings and performs all actions, is the vehicle of consciousness; it is fivefold and again tenfold.

original.text: vajrajāpasthito mantrī cittanidhyaptimāpnuyāt | mayopamasamādhistho bhūtakoṭyāṃ samāviśet || bhūtakoṭeḥ samuttiṣṭhannadvayajñānamāpnuyāt | yuganadvasamādhistho na kiñcicchakṣate punaḥ ||

paraphrase: Established in vajra recitation, the mantrin attains mind-isolation; abiding in the illusion-like samādhi he enters the reality-limit; rising from it he attains non-dual gnosis; abiding in the samādhi of union he has nothing more to learn; this is called the perfected yoga, he is the great Vajradhara, omniscient, and sees the three times in an instant through the purity of clear light.

original.text: etattattvaṃ sthitaṃ tantre śrīsamāje sumudritam | vyākhyātantrānusāreṇa boddhavyaṃ guruvaktrataḥ ||

paraphrase: This reality, well sealed in the glorious Samāja, is to be understood according to the explanatory tantras and from the guru's mouth.

original.text: yathā jalaṃ jale nyastaṃ ghṛtaṃ caiva yathā ghṛte | svakīyaṃ ca svayaṃ paśyej jñānaṃ yatreha vandanā ||

paraphrase: As water placed in water and ghee in ghee, one sees one's own gnosis by itself — that is the homage here.

original.text: etāḥ prakṛtayaḥ sūkṣmāḥ śataṃ ṣaṣṭyuttaraṃ divā | rātrau cāpi pravartante vāyuvāhanahetunā ||

paraphrase: The very empty (light-appearance, ālokābhāsa) has forty natural concepts (passion, delight, joy, amazement, embrace, courage, pride, violence, deceit and others), called 'day', the sun; the great empty (light-attainment, ālokopalabdhi) has seven moments of ignorance (forgetting, confusion, silence, weariness, laziness, dullness); these subtle natures, one hundred and sixty, run day and night by the movement of the wind.
notes: The text gives 33 + 40 + 7 natures (80) and speaks of 160 subtle natures by day and night.

original.text: śūnyaṃ ca atiśūnyaṃ ca mahāśunyaṃ tṛtīyakam | caturthaṃ sarvaśūnyaṃ ca phalahetuprabhedataḥ ||

paraphrase: The empty, the very empty, the great empty third, and the fourth, the all-empty — distinguished as result and cause.

original.text: prajñopāyasamāyogānniṣpannamupalabdhakam | upalabdhācca niṣpannāt sarvaśūnyaṃ prabhāsvaram ||

paraphrase: From the union of wisdom and means comes the 'perfected' and the 'attained'; from the attained and perfected comes the all-empty, clear light.

original.text: ālokaśśūnyaṃ prajñā ca cittaṃ ca paratantrakam | tasyedānīṃ pravakṣyāmi prakṛtispharaṇaṃ sphuṭam || trayastriṃśat prakṛtayaḥ svasaṃvedyāḥ śarīriṇām | saṃvṛtisphuṭarupeṇa niśāsañjñā pradarśitāḥ ||
original.edition: Pañcakrama, GRETIL/DSBC e-text based on R. S. Tripathi's ed. (Sarnath 2001) (IAST by the unit)

paraphrase: The first empty is light (āloka), wisdom and the dependent mind; its natures, the thirty-three natural concepts (detachment, the middling, the intense, mind's coming and going, grief …, fear, craving, hunger, thirst, feeling, compassion, doubt, envy and so on), are known by every embodied being and are shown conventionally as 'night'.
notes: Original quotes vv. 7 and 12 only; the list in vv. 8–11 is summarized.

original.text: svādhiṣṭhānakramo nāma saṃvṛteḥ satyadarśanam | gurupādaprasādena labhyate tacca nānyathā || svādhiṣṭhānakramaṃ labdhvā sarvabuddhāmayaḥ prabhuḥ | janmanīhaiva buddhatvaṃ niḥsandehaṃ prapadyate ||

paraphrase: The stage of self-consecration shows conventional truth; it is obtained through the grace of the guru's feet and not otherwise; for the practitioner who does not obtain it, labour in sūtras, tantras and rituals is in vain; obtaining it, he attains buddhahood in this very birth without doubt.

original.text: svādhiṣṭhānasamādhiśca prabhāsvarapadaṃ tathā | satyadvayamiti khyātaṃ phalahetuviśeṣataḥ ||
original.edition: Pañcakrama, GRETIL/DSBC e-text based on R. S. Tripathi's ed. (Sarnath 2001) (IAST by the unit)
original.licence: GRETIL/DSBC e-text quoted for reference; terms of use as for the source file

paraphrase: The samādhi of self-consecration and the state of clear light are known as the two truths, distinguished as result and cause; clear light is attained after self-consecration, so the vajra guru first shows self-consecration.

original.text: asvatantraṃ jagat sarvaṃ svatantraṃ naiva jāyate | hetuḥ prabhāsvaraṃ tasya sarvaśūnyaṃ prabhāsvaram || yena cittena bālāśca saṃsāre bandhanaṃ gatāḥ | yoginastena cittena sugatānāṃ gatiṃ gatāḥ ||
original.edition: Pañcakrama, GRETIL/DSBC e-text based on R. S. Tripathi's ed. (Sarnath 2001) (IAST by the unit)

paraphrase: The whole world is dependent, nothing independent arises; its cause is clear light, and the all-empty is clear light; by the same mind through which fools are bound in saṃsāra, yogins go to the state of the sugatas; here no one is born and no one dies; saṃsāra is to be known as standing in the shape of mind.

original.text: asau svayambhūrbhagavān eka evādhidaivataḥ | upadeśapradānāt tu vajrācāryo 'dhikastataḥ ||
original.edition: Pañcakrama, GRETIL/DSBC e-text based on R. S. Tripathi's ed. (Sarnath 2001) (IAST by the unit)
original.licence: GRETIL/DSBC e-text quoted for reference; terms of use as for the source file

paraphrase: The Self-born Lord is the sole supreme deity, but because he gives the instruction the vajra master is greater than he.

original.text: jñātvā krameṇa tattvajñaḥ svādhiṣṭhānaprabhāsvaram | tayoreva samājaṃ yad yuganaddhakramo hyayam || saṃvṛtiṃ paramārthaṃ ca pṛthag jñātvā vibhāgataḥ | sammīlanaṃ bhaved yatra yuganaddhaṃ taducyate ||

paraphrase: Knowing in sequence self-consecration and clear light, their joining is the stage of union; knowing conventional and ultimate separately and then their blending is union.

original.text: saṃsāro nirvṛtiśceti kalpanādvayavarjanāt | ekībhāvo bhaved yatra yuganaddhaṃ taducyate || grāhyaṃ ca grāhakaṃ caiva dvidhā buddhirna vidyate | abhinnatā bhaved yatra tadāha yuganaddhakam ||

original.licence: GRETIL/DSBC e-text quoted for reference; terms of use as for the source file

paraphrase: Where saṃsāra and nirvāṇa become one by abandoning the two concepts, that is called union; who knows defilement and purification as one in the ultimate knows union; who joins the conception of form and of formlessness knows union; where grasped and grasper are not two, that is union.

original.text: utpattikrama eko 'yam utpannakrama ityapi | ekatvaṃ tu dvayoryatra yuganaddhastaducyate ||
original.edition: Pañcakrama, GRETIL/DSBC e-text based on R. S. Tripathi's ed. (Sarnath 2001) (IAST by the unit)
original.licence: GRETIL/DSBC e-text quoted for reference; terms of use as for the source file

paraphrase: The generation stage is one and the completion stage another; where the two become one, that is called union.

original.text: etadevādvayaṃ jñānam apratiṣṭhitanirvṛtiḥ | buddhatvaṃ vajrasattvatvaṃ sarvaiśvaryaṃ tathaiva ca ||
original.edition: Pañcakrama, GRETIL/DSBC e-text based on R. S. Tripathi's ed. (Sarnath 2001) (IAST by the unit)
original.licence: GRETIL/DSBC e-text quoted for reference; terms of use as for the source file

paraphrase: This itself is non-dual gnosis, non-abiding nirvāṇa, buddhahood, Vajrasattva-hood and all sovereignty.

original.text: anutpādādayaḥ śabdā advayajñānasūcakāḥ | asyaiva vācakāḥ sarve nānyat tatrābhidhīyate || mahāmudrātmikāṃ siddhiṃ sadasatpakṣavarjitām | anenaiva gatā buddhā gaṅgāyāḥ sikatopamāḥ ||

paraphrase: Words such as 'unborn' point to non-dual gnosis and denote only it; by this alone the buddhas, numerous as the sands of the Gaṅgā, went to the attainment of mahāmudrā, beyond the positions of being and non-being.

original.text: yathātmani tathā śatrau yathā bhāryā tathātmajā | yathā mātā tathā vaiśyā yathā ḍombī tathā dvijā || evaṃ jñātvā cared jñānī nirviśaṅkastu sarvakṛt | pracchannavratamāsādya sidhyante sarvasampadaḥ ||
original.edition: Pañcakrama, GRETIL/DSBC e-text based on R. S. Tripathi's ed. (Sarnath 2001) (IAST by the unit)
original.licence: GRETIL/DSBC e-text quoted for reference; terms of use as for the source file

paraphrase: The great yogin established in union should meditate on union and the conduct that goes with it: as oneself so the enemy, as wife so daughter, as mother so courtesan, as the outcaste woman so the brahmin woman, as cloth so hide, as jewel so chaff, as urine so wine, as food so excrement, as praise so abuse, as Rudra so the Vajrī, as night so day, as pleasure so pain, as hell so heaven; knowing thus the wise one acts without hesitation, and by keeping the hidden observance all attainments are accomplished.
notes: Only for one established in union, per v. 29; the observance is 'hidden' (pracchannavrata).

original.text: prajñākaruṇayoraikyaṃ jñātvā yatra pravartate | yuganaddha iti khyātaḥ kramo 'yaṃ buddhagocaraḥ ||
original.edition: Pañcakrama, GRETIL/DSBC e-text based on R. S. Tripathi's ed. (Sarnath 2001) (IAST by the unit)
original.licence: GRETIL/DSBC e-text quoted for reference; terms of use as for the source file

paraphrase: Where one proceeds knowing the unity of wisdom and compassion, that stage, the domain of the buddhas, is called union.
